metadata.title: Cybernetics and VSM Foundations — Sources
metadata.description: Primary texts and references for 11 cybernetics and VSM primitives: feedback loops, Ashby's Law, VSM systems 1–5, S3*, recursion levels, variety engineering, and algedonic channels

primary_texts.name: Brain of the Firm
primary_texts.description: Beer, S. (1972, 2nd ed. 1981). Allen Lane / Wiley. Canonical VSM definition: Systems 1–5, algedonic channels, recursion principle. Primary source for primitives #3–#8, #11.

primary_texts.name: Heart of Enterprise
primary_texts.description: Beer, S. (1979). Wiley. Variety engineering, amplifiers, attenuators, and transducers. Management of complexity. Primary source for primitives #2, #10.

primary_texts.name: Diagnosing the System for Organizations
primary_texts.description: Beer, S. (1985). Wiley. Practical VSM application guide with diagnostic exercises. Primary source for all VSM system primitives and the system-in-focus concept.

primary_texts.name: An Introduction to Cybernetics
primary_texts.description: Ashby, W.R. (1956). Chapman & Hall. Law of Requisite Variety (ch. 11), homeostasis, and variety. Primary source for primitive #2.

primary_texts.name: Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine
primary_texts.description: Wiener, N. (1948, 2nd ed. 1961). MIT Press. Feedback, negative feedback as purposive behaviour, and the foundations of cybernetics. Primary source for primitive #1.

primary_texts.name: Every Good Regulator of a System Must Be a Model of That System
primary_texts.description: Conant, R.C., & Ashby, W.R. (1970). International Journal of Systems Science, 1(2), 89–97. Good regulator theorem — foundational support for Ashby's Law (primitive #2) and the necessity of internal modelling.

primary_texts.name: A Complexity Approach to Sustainability
primary_texts.description: Espinosa, A., & Walker, J. (2011). Imperial College Press. VSM applied to sustainability and complex real-world systems. Source for VSM practice references across all primitives.

primary_texts.name: Intelligent Organizations
primary_texts.description: Schwaninger, M. (2006). Springer. VSM, management cybernetics, and intelligent organisation design. Secondary source for S3/S4 interface (primitive #5, #7) and identity (primitive #8).

primary_texts.name: The Fractal Organization
primary_texts.description: Hoverstadt, P. (2009). Wiley. Practitioner-oriented VSM with recursion patterns, S3* implementation, and algedonic channel design. Secondary source for all VSM primitives.

primary_texts.name: Business Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World
primary_texts.description: Sterman, J.D. (2000). McGraw-Hill. Feedback loop notation, causal loop diagrams, delay analysis, and oscillation dynamics. Secondary source for primitive #1.

primary_texts.name: Autopoiesis and Cognition
primary_texts.description: Maturana, H.R., & Varela, F.J. (1980). Reidel. Autopoiesis — self-production and closure in viable systems. Theoretical background for S5 identity closure (primitive #8) and recursion (primitive #9).

primary_texts.name: Systems Thinking: Creative Holism for Managers
primary_texts.description: Jackson, M.C. (2003). Wiley. Overview of systems methodologies including VSM in the context of management cybernetics. Useful secondary source for contextualising Beer's work.

primary_texts.name: VSM Guide — A Practical Guide to the Viable System Model
primary_texts.description: Pemberton, J. (2020). Practitioner guide for applying VSM in organisations. Useful supplementary reference for recursion levels and S3* audit in contemporary organisations.

primary_texts.name: Beyond Dispute: The Invention of Team Syntegrity
primary_texts.description: Beer, S. (1994). Wiley. Beer's later work on syntegration and participatory decision-making. Background for S4 intelligence and S5 governance design.

primary_texts.name: Revisiting the Viable System Model as an emancipatory systems approach
primary_texts.description: Espinosa, A. (2025). Systems Research and Behavioral Science, 42(1), 171–188. DOI: 10.1002/sres.3090. Argues VSM is an emancipatory rather than purely functionalist model; addresses Jackson's critiques. Empirical grounding via Colombia community case study (see Espinosa & Martinez-Lozada 2025). Relevant to primitives #3, #8, #9.

primary_texts.name: The Viable System Model to Support Sustainable Self-Governance in Communities: Learning from Case Studies
primary_texts.description: Espinosa, A., & Martinez-Lozada, A. (2025). Systemic Practice and Action Research. DOI: 10.1007/s11213-025-09724-3. Empirical VSM application to community self-governance in Colombia; demonstrates VSM-guided S1–S5 design enables durable self-funded community projects. Corroborates Espinosa2025SRBS. Relevant to primitives #3, #8, #9.

primary_texts.name: Variety Engineering – A Cybernetic Concept with Practical Implications
primary_texts.description: Schwaninger, M., & Ott, S.C. (2025). In: EUROCAST 2024. LNCS vol. 15173, Springer. DOI: 10.1007/978-3-031-82957-4_21. Formalises Variety Engineering as mutual complexity amplification/attenuation; illustrates with ecological, social, economic cases. Updated version of SRBS 2023 article. Relevant to primitive #10.

primary_texts.name: The Agent Use of Agent Beings: Agent Cybernetics Is the Missing Science of Foundation Agents
primary_texts.description: Wang, X., Yang, C., Zhao, H., Lin, Z., & Hu, S. (2026). arXiv:2605.10754 [cs.AI]. Maps six canonical laws of classical cybernetics (including Ashby's Law of Requisite Variety and the Good Regulator theorem) onto six agent design principles, synthesising three engineering desiderata: reliability, lifelong running, and self-improvement. Evidence grade: C (preprint, no peer review; conceptual framework). Relevant to primitive #2 (Ashby's Law), Agent-Team Topology Audit recipe.

primary_texts.name: Agentic AI Needs a Systems Theory
primary_texts.description: Miehling, E., Ramamurthy, K.N., Varshney, K.R., et al. (2025). arXiv:2503.00237 [cs.AI]. Argues advanced AI agent development requires a systems-theoretic perspective; interactions between agents and environment produce emergent capabilities not apparent from isolated components. Cites Ashby and Wiener. Corroborates AgentCybernetics2026 from a different entry point. Evidence grade: C (preprint). Relevant to primitives #1, #2.

primary_texts.name: The Viable System Model Through a Power-Relations Lens: Towards a Power-Aware Conceptual Framework
primary_texts.description: Zeini, N. (2026, early online). Systems Research and Behavioral Science. DOI: 10.1002/sres.70028. Critiques VSM's limited engagement with power relations; proposes integrating Beer's VSM with Gaventa's power-cube framework to produce a power-aware VSM diagnostic layer (visible/hidden/invisible power × local/national/global levels). Evidence grade: B (peer-reviewed journal; conceptual extension with case application). Relevant to Known Traps: Power-blind trap.

primary_texts.name: The Viable System Model and the Taxonomy of Organizational Pathologies in the Age of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
primary_texts.description: Perez Rios, J. (2025). Systems, 13(9), 749. MDPI. DOI: 10.3390/systems13090749. Applies VSM together with Perez Rios's Taxonomy of Organizational Pathologies (TOP) to AI governance risks; maps 13 organisational pathologies to VSM systems and AI-advancement failure modes. Evidence grade: B (peer-reviewed journal; conceptual/applied paper). Relevant to VSM Pathology Checklist for AI Systems.

primary_texts.name: Cybernetic Revolutionaries: Technology and Politics in Allende's Chile
primary_texts.description: Medina, E. (2011). MIT Press. Primary archival history of Project Cybersyn (Chile, 1971-1973) — Stafford Beer's real-world VSM deployment. Documents the actual scope (telex network + one mainframe, not networked real-time control), the October 1972 truckers'-strike operational use, partial rollout (~26.7% of nationalized firms by May 1973), and the project's end after the 11 September 1973 coup. Corrects the popular 'real-time control room ran the economy' myth. Evidence grade: A (peer-reviewed academic monograph, primary archival research). Relevant to Historical Grounding: Project Cybersyn in patterns-scenarios-traps.md.

primary_texts.name: A Formal Definition of Scale-Dependent Complexity and the Multi-Scale Law of Requisite Variety
primary_texts.description: Siegenfeld, A.F., & Bar-Yam, Y. (2025). Entropy, 27(8), 835. MDPI. DOI: 10.3390/e27080835 (PMC-indexed as PMC12385218). Proposes a multi-scale generalisation of Ashby's Law showing that variety requirements and regulator capacity are scale-dependent. Implies that in hierarchical or recursive systems (including nested agent architectures), variety analysis must be performed at each recursion level independently rather than once for the whole. Evidence grade: B (peer-reviewed journal; PMC-indexed). Relevant to primitive #2 (Ashby's Law), primitive #9 (Recursion Levels), and Agent-Team Topology Audit recipe.

primary_texts.name: The CASE Framework: A Multi-Disciplinary Control Architecture for Governing Enterprise Agentic AI
primary_texts.description: Telukunta, S., Lilis, G.N., & Baron, L. (2026). arXiv:2608.10153 [cs.AI], submitted 10 August 2026. Four-layer governance architecture (control / complex adaptive systems / supervisory cybernetics / SRE) for enterprise agent fleets. Explicitly operationalises Beer's VSM — recursion as federated supervision, and the algedonic channel as a severity signal that skips escalation tiers to page accountable authority unfiltered. Formalises human oversight as V_human x G >= V_agents, where G is engineered amplification gain, evaluated at peak behavioural variety, converting EU AI Act Article 14 obligations into a falsifiable design condition with named artefacts (variety budgets, amplification chains, escalation SLAs). Evidence grade: C (preprint, no peer review) for the CASE architecture; the underlying cybernetic condition rests on grade-A sources (Ashby1956, Conant1970, Beer1979). Relevant to primitive #2, #10, #11, and the Agent-Team Topology Audit recipe.

primary_texts.name: From Runtime Records to Legal Findings: An Evidentiary-Adequacy Criterion for Agentic AI Oversight
primary_texts.description: Janssen, J. (2026). arXiv:2607.00941 [cs.AI], submitted 1 July 2026. Proposes an evidentiary-adequacy criterion for agentic AI oversight, relating the argument to requisite variety, the Good Regulator theorem, and the trace-versus-hyperproperty boundary of runtime verification. Reaches the ceremonial-oversight conclusion from a legal/evidentiary entry point rather than an architectural one, so corroborates TelukuntaCASE2026 independently. Evidence grade: C (preprint, no peer review). Relevant to primitive #2 (Ashby's Law) and the ceremonial-oversight trap in patterns-scenarios-traps.md.
